quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'I work in a bank.'
options: He said he worked in a bank.
He said he works in a bank.
He said that I worked in a bank.
quests.correctAnswer: He said he worked in a bank.
quests.sentence: He said, 'I work in a bank.'
quests.hint: Present simple ('work') shifts to past simple ('worked') in reported speech.
quests.explanation: 'Work' (present simple) becomes 'worked' (past simple). The pronoun 'I' shifts to 'he'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I don't eat red meat.'
options: She said she didn't eat red meat.
She said she doesn't eat red meat.
She said she hadn't eaten red meat.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she didn't eat red meat.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I don't eat red meat.'
quests.hint: 'Don't eat' (negative present simple) shifts to 'didn't eat' (negative past simple).
quests.explanation: Negative present simple ('don't eat') shifts to negative past simple ('didn't eat') in reported speech.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: Mum said, 'Come inside before it rains.'
options: Mum told me to come inside before it rained.
Mum said me to come inside before it rained.
Mum told me to come inside before it rains.
quests.correctAnswer: Mum told me to come inside before it rained.
quests.sentence: Mum said, 'Come inside before it rains.'
quests.hint: The imperative is reported as 'told + object + to + infinitive'. The verb in the subordinate clause also shifts.
quests.explanation: The imperative 'Come inside' becomes 'told me to come inside'. The conditional verb 'rains' shifts to 'rained'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'I'll be there by 7 o'clock.'
options: He promised he would be there by 7 o'clock.
He promised he will be there by 7 o'clock.
He promised he would have been there by 7 o'clock.
quests.correctAnswer: He promised he would be there by 7 o'clock.
quests.sentence: He said, 'I'll be there by 7 o'clock.'
quests.hint: 'Will' shifts to 'would'. Promises are naturally reported with 'promised'.
quests.explanation: 'I'll' (I will) becomes 'would'. The verb 'said' can be replaced by 'promised' to convey the speaker's intention.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'Are you coming to the party?'
options: She asked if I was coming to the party.
She asked if I am coming to the party.
She asked was I coming to the party.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked if I was coming to the party.
quests.sentence: She asked, 'Are you coming to the party?'
quests.hint: Yes/No questions use 'if'. 'Are' shifts to 'was'. Statement word order is used.
quests.explanation: Yes/No questions in reported speech use 'if' followed by statement word order. 'Are coming' → 'was coming'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'I don't understand the instructions.'
options: He said he didn't understand the instructions.
He said he doesn't understand the instructions.
He said he hadn't understood the instructions.
quests.correctAnswer: He said he didn't understand the instructions.
quests.sentence: He said, 'I don't understand the instructions.'
quests.hint: 'Don't understand' shifts to 'didn't understand'.
quests.explanation: Present simple negative 'don't understand' becomes past simple negative 'didn't understand' in reported speech.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'Where do you buy your groceries?'
options: She asked where I bought my groceries.
She asked where do I buy my groceries.
She asked where I buy my groceries.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked where I bought my groceries.
quests.sentence: She asked, 'Where do you buy your groceries?'
quests.hint: Wh-questions use statement word order. 'Do' disappears and 'buy' shifts to 'bought'.
quests.explanation: In reported wh-questions, drop the auxiliary 'do' and use statement order. 'Buy' shifts to 'bought', 'your' shifts to 'my'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'I can speak three languages.'
options: He said he could speak three languages.
He said he can speak three languages.
He said he speaks three languages.
quests.correctAnswer: He said he could speak three languages.
quests.sentence: He said, 'I can speak three languages.'
quests.hint: 'Can' shifts to 'could' in reported speech.
quests.explanation: 'Can' becomes 'could' in reported speech. The pronoun 'I' shifts to 'he'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The teacher said, 'Don't run on the stairs.'
options: The teacher told us not to run on the stairs.
The teacher told us to not running on the stairs.
The teacher said don't run on the stairs.
quests.correctAnswer: The teacher told us not to run on the stairs.
quests.sentence: The teacher said, 'Don't run on the stairs.'
quests.hint: Negative imperatives are reported with 'told + object + not to + infinitive'.
quests.explanation: Negative commands use 'told + object + not to + infinitive'. 'Don't run' becomes 'not to run'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I have broken my phone.'
options: She said she had broken her phone.
She said she has broken her phone.
She said she broke her phone.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she had broken her phone.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I have broken my phone.'
quests.hint: Present perfect ('have broken') shifts to past perfect ('had broken'). Pronouns also shift.
quests.explanation: 'Have broken' (present perfect) becomes 'had broken' (past perfect). 'I' → 'she', 'my' → 'her'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: They said, 'We went to Rome last summer.'
options: They said they had gone to Rome the previous summer.
They said they went to Rome last summer.
They said they have gone to Rome the previous summer.
quests.correctAnswer: They said they had gone to Rome the previous summer.
quests.sentence: They said, 'We went to Rome last summer.'
quests.hint: Past simple ('went') shifts to past perfect ('had gone'). 'Last' shifts to 'the previous'.
quests.explanation: 'Went' (past simple) shifts to 'had gone' (past perfect). 'Last summer' becomes 'the previous summer'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He asked, 'Do you know where the post office is?'
options: He asked if I knew where the post office was.
He asked do I know where the post office is.
He asked if I know where the post office is.
quests.correctAnswer: He asked if I knew where the post office was.
quests.sentence: He asked, 'Do you know where the post office is?'
quests.hint: Yes/No question with embedded question. Both verbs shift. Use 'if' and statement order.
quests.explanation: 'Do you know' → 'if I knew' (tense shift + statement order). 'Is' in the embedded clause also shifts to 'was'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'My children are playing in the garden.'
options: She said her children were playing in the garden.
She said her children are playing in the garden.
She said my children were playing in the garden.
quests.correctAnswer: She said her children were playing in the garden.
quests.sentence: She said, 'My children are playing in the garden.'
quests.hint: Present continuous ('are playing') shifts to past continuous ('were playing'). 'My' shifts to 'her'.
quests.explanation: 'Are playing' becomes 'were playing'. The possessive 'my' shifts to 'her'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He asked, 'What are you looking for?'
options: He asked what I was looking for.
He asked what are you looking for.
He asked what I am looking for.
quests.correctAnswer: He asked what I was looking for.
quests.sentence: He asked, 'What are you looking for?'
quests.hint: Wh-question: use statement order and shift tense. 'Are looking' → 'was looking'.
quests.explanation: In reported wh-questions, use statement word order and shift the tense. 'Are looking' becomes 'was looking'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: Dad said, 'Pack your bag and get ready.'
options: Dad told me to pack my bag and get ready.
Dad said pack your bag and get ready.
Dad told me pack my bag and get ready.
quests.correctAnswer: Dad told me to pack my bag and get ready.
quests.sentence: Dad said, 'Pack your bag and get ready.'
quests.hint: Double imperative: both verbs reported as 'to pack... and get ready'. Pronoun shifts.
quests.explanation: Both imperatives use 'to + infinitive'. 'Your bag' becomes 'my bag' as the perspective shifts to the listener.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I must take this medicine twice a day.'
options: She said she had to take that medicine twice a day.
She said she must take this medicine twice a day.
She said she must take that medicine twice a day.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she had to take that medicine twice a day.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I must take this medicine twice a day.'
quests.hint: 'Must' → 'had to', 'this' → 'that', 'I' → 'she'.
quests.explanation: 'Must' shifts to 'had to'. The deictic 'this' shifts to 'that'. The pronoun 'I' becomes 'she'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He asked, 'May I sit here?'
options: He asked whether he might sit there.
He asked if he may sit there.
He asked whether he might sit here.
quests.correctAnswer: He asked whether he might sit there.
quests.sentence: He asked, 'May I sit here?'
quests.hint: 'May' shifts to 'might', 'I' → 'he', and 'here' → 'there'. Use 'whether' or 'if'.
quests.explanation: 'May' shifts to 'might', 'I' becomes 'he', and 'here' becomes 'there'. Both 'whether' and 'if' are acceptable.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I saw the accident three days ago.'
options: She said she had seen the accident three days before.
She said she saw the accident three days ago.
She said she had seen the accident three days ago.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she had seen the accident three days before.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I saw the accident three days ago.'
quests.hint: 'Saw' shifts to 'had seen'. 'Ago' shifts to 'before'.
quests.explanation: 'Saw' (past simple) shifts to 'had seen' (past perfect). 'Ago' becomes 'before' in reported speech.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'There will be a big storm tonight.'
options: He said there would be a big storm that night.
He said there will be a big storm tonight.
He said there would be a big storm tonight.
quests.correctAnswer: He said there would be a big storm that night.
quests.sentence: He said, 'There will be a big storm tonight.'
quests.hint: 'Will' shifts to 'would'. 'Tonight' shifts to 'that night'.
quests.explanation: 'Will be' becomes 'would be'. The time word 'tonight' shifts to 'that night'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'Have you ever been to Japan?'
options: She asked if I had ever been to Japan.
She asked if I have ever been to Japan.
She asked had I ever been to Japan.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked if I had ever been to Japan.
quests.sentence: She asked, 'Have you ever been to Japan?'
quests.hint: Yes/No question: use 'if', statement order, shift present perfect to past perfect.
quests.explanation: Present perfect 'have been' shifts to past perfect 'had been'. Use 'if' and statement word order.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The teacher said, 'Stand in a line and wait your turn.'
options: The teacher told the students to stand in a line and wait their turn.
The teacher said that the students stand in a line and wait their turn.
The teacher told the students stand in a line and wait their turn.
quests.correctAnswer: The teacher told the students to stand in a line and wait their turn.
quests.sentence: The teacher said, 'Stand in a line and wait your turn.'
quests.hint: Double imperative: 'told + object + to + infinitive' for both verbs. 'Your' shifts to 'their'.
quests.explanation: Both imperatives are reported with 'to + infinitive'. 'Your turn' shifts to 'their turn'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I am meeting my boss at noon.'
options: She said she was meeting her boss at noon.
She said she is meeting her boss at noon.
She said she was meeting my boss at noon.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she was meeting her boss at noon.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I am meeting my boss at noon.'
quests.hint: Present continuous shifts to past continuous. 'My' shifts to 'her'.
quests.explanation: 'Am meeting' becomes 'was meeting'. The possessive 'my' shifts to 'her'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He asked, 'When does the supermarket close?'
options: He asked when the supermarket closed.
He asked when does the supermarket close.
He asked when the supermarket closes.
quests.correctAnswer: He asked when the supermarket closed.
quests.sentence: He asked, 'When does the supermarket close?'
quests.hint: Wh-question: statement order, no 'does', and 'close' shifts to 'closed'.
quests.explanation: Drop the auxiliary 'does', use statement order, and shift 'close' to 'closed'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The doctor said, 'You should get more sleep.'
options: The doctor advised me to get more sleep.
The doctor advised me that I should get more sleep.
The doctor told me getting more sleep.
quests.correctAnswer: The doctor advised me to get more sleep.
quests.sentence: The doctor said, 'You should get more sleep.'
quests.hint: Advice with 'should' is best reported as 'advised + object + to + infinitive'.
quests.explanation: 'You should get more sleep' is a piece of advice. It is most naturally reported as 'advised me to get more sleep'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: They said, 'We haven't decided yet.'
options: They said they hadn't decided yet.
They said they haven't decided yet.
They said they didn't decide yet.
quests.correctAnswer: They said they hadn't decided yet.
quests.sentence: They said, 'We haven't decided yet.'
quests.hint: Present perfect negative ('haven't decided') shifts to past perfect negative ('hadn't decided').
quests.explanation: 'Haven't decided' (present perfect) shifts to 'hadn't decided' (past perfect) in reported speech.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He asked, 'How did you get here so quickly?'
options: He asked how I had got there so quickly.
He asked how I got here so quickly.
He asked how did I get there so quickly.
quests.correctAnswer: He asked how I had got there so quickly.
quests.sentence: He asked, 'How did you get here so quickly?'
quests.hint: Wh-question: drop 'did', use statement order, backshift tense, and shift 'here' to 'there'.
quests.explanation: Drop 'did', use statement word order, shift 'got' to 'had got', and change 'here' to 'there'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'Would you mind closing the window?'
options: She asked me to close the window.
She asked me if I would mind to close the window.
She told me closing the window.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked me to close the window.
quests.sentence: She said, 'Would you mind closing the window?'
quests.hint: 'Would you mind...?' is a polite request reported as 'asked + object + to + infinitive'.
quests.explanation: 'Would you mind closing the window?' is a polite request. The most natural reported form is 'asked me to close the window'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'I can't remember where I put my wallet.'
options: He said he couldn't remember where he had put his wallet.
He said he can't remember where he put his wallet.
He said he couldn't remember where I put my wallet.
quests.correctAnswer: He said he couldn't remember where he had put his wallet.
quests.sentence: He said, 'I can't remember where I put my wallet.'
quests.hint: 'Can't' → 'couldn't', 'put' → 'had put', 'I/my' → 'he/his'.
quests.explanation: 'Can't' becomes 'couldn't'. 'Put' (past simple in embedded clause) shifts to 'had put'. Pronouns 'I' → 'he', 'my' → 'his'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'Did anyone see what happened?'
options: She asked if anyone had seen what had happened.
She asked if anyone saw what happened.
She asked did anyone see what happened.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked if anyone had seen what had happened.
quests.sentence: She asked, 'Did anyone see what happened?'
quests.hint: Yes/No question: 'did' disappears, both verbs shift back, and 'if' is added.
quests.explanation: 'Did' disappears. 'See' shifts to 'had seen' and 'happened' shifts to 'had happened'. Use 'if' and statement order.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'I want to go back to university.'
options: He said he wanted to go back to university.
He said he wants to go back to university.
He said he had wanted to go back to university.
quests.correctAnswer: He said he wanted to go back to university.
quests.sentence: He said, 'I want to go back to university.'
quests.hint: 'Want' (present simple) shifts to 'wanted' (past simple).
quests.explanation: 'Want' becomes 'wanted' in reported speech. The pronoun 'I' shifts to 'he'.
